Retract the landmarks of a photograph (it goes back to "not measured")

Source: R/landmark_journal.R
retract_landmarks.Rd

The journal is append-only and is the source of truth: deleting a row of the workbook would not stand, since the digitizer rebuilds the workbook from the journal. A measurement is therefore withdrawn by APPENDING a retraction record for each of its keys (mode = "retracted"); consolidate_landmarks() then leaves those keys out, so the photograph is "to measure" again everywhere – the digitizer's "new" queue, measure_queue(), the workbook rebuilt from the journal. Nothing is erased: the earlier records stay in the journal and landmark_journal_history() shows them, retraction included. A later digitization of the same key simply supersedes the retraction.

Usage

retract_landmarks(
  journal_dir,
  photo = NULL,
  row_key = NULL,
  xlsx_path = NULL,
  operator = NULL
)

Arguments

journal_dir

Landmark journal directory.

photo

Photograph code(s) (file name without extension): every live key recorded on that photograph is retracted – all the individuals of a plate, all the repeats.

row_key

Key(s) to retract directly, in addition to photo.

xlsx_path

Optional workbook of digitize_landmarks(): the rows of the retracted specimens are removed from every sheet now (atomic write, the previous file kept as .prev.xlsx), rather than at the next rebuild. Do not run this while a digitizer has that workbook open: it would write its own copy back.

operator

Who retracts (recorded in the journal).

Value

Invisibly, a data.frame of the retracted keys (row_key, specimen, photo_file); zero rows when nothing was measured.

Details

Typical use: the prepared image of a measured photograph has been re-cropped or turned, so its landmarks, which are in the pixels of that image, no longer fall on the fish.

See also

consolidate_landmarks(), landmark_journal_history()

Examples

d <- file.path(tempdir(), "retract_demo")
jr <- landmark_journal_open(d, operator = "AT")
#> Session journal: /tmp/RtmpFjKqwk/retract_demo/landmarks_AT_20261027T065942Z.tsv
landmark_journal_append(jr, "fish_01", cbind(c(10, 20), c(5, 6)), 1:2,
                        specimen = "fish_01", photo_file = "fish_01.jpg")
nrow(consolidate_landmarks(d))          # 1
#> [1] 1
retract_landmarks(d, photo = "fish_01")
#> Session journal: /tmp/RtmpFjKqwk/retract_demo/landmarks_runner_20261027T065942Z.tsv
#> 1 measurement(s) retracted: fish_01.
nrow(consolidate_landmarks(d))          # 0
#> [1] 0
unlink(d, recursive = TRUE)
